questions.clue: A description of the current situation that contains the information needed to evaluate future actions.
questions.explanation: The state records the facts the planner needs to decide what can happen next.
questions.reference: Stanford CS 221 teaching notes, States-based Models, Search optimization and Tree search. https://web.stanford.edu/~shervine/teaching/cs-221/cheatsheet-states-models/

questions.clue: The known outcome a supervised model is trained to predict for each example.
questions.explanation: The label provides the outcome against which the training prediction can be compared.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §2.1.4, Supervised Versus Unsupervised Learning. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue: The training examples have input variables but no provided outcome to predict.
questions.explanation: Unsupervised methods look for structure in the inputs without provided target outcomes.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §2.1.4, Supervised Versus Unsupervised Learning. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue: Split text into units a language model can map to vocabulary IDs.
questions.explanation: A tokenizer maps text to a sequence of tokens, often subword pieces.
questions.reference: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing, 3rd ed. draft (August 2026), Ch. 2, Words and Tokens. https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/2.pdf

questions.clue: A separate portion of the data is reserved for the final evaluation after all tuning is done.
questions.explanation: An untouched test set estimates how the finished model performs on unseen examples.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Datasets: Dividing the original dataset, Dividing the original dataset. https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/overfitting/dividing-datasets

questions.clue: A neural network layer sits between the input and the output.
questions.explanation: A hidden layer transforms intermediate representations before later layers use them.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Neural networks: Nodes and hidden layers, Implementing a hidden layer. https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/neural-networks/nodes-hidden-layers

questions.clue: A maze solver explores all routes one step from the start before examining routes two steps away.
questions.explanation: Breadth-first search expands the shallowest available nodes first.
questions.reference: Stanford CS 221 teaching notes, States-based Models, Search optimization and Tree search. https://web.stanford.edu/~shervine/teaching/cs-221/cheatsheet-states-models/

questions.clue: A model predicts the next day’s energy use in kilowatt-hours from past readings and weather.
questions.explanation: Predicting a numerical response is a regression task.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §2.1.5, Regression Versus Classification Problems. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue: To label a new plant, vote among the labels of its k nearest plants in the training data.
questions.explanation: The class prediction comes from nearby labeled training examples.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §2.2.3, The Classification Setting, K-Nearest Neighbors. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue: Group unlabeled songs by similar tempo and loudness without specifying target groups beforehand.
questions.explanation: Clustering groups observations using similarity in their measured features.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §12.4, Clustering Methods. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue: Several model settings are tried. Which data can choose among them while leaving a separate test set untouched?
questions.explanation: Validation scores inform tuning while the test set remains available for final evaluation.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Datasets: Dividing the original dataset, Dividing the original dataset. https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/overfitting/dividing-datasets

questions.clue: Split homes repeatedly by feature thresholds, then predict sale price by the average price in each terminal region.
questions.explanation: A regression tree partitions the feature space and can predict each region’s mean response.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §8.1.1, Regression Trees. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue:
(TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN)
Confusion-matrix counts.
questions.explanation: Accuracy is the fraction of all predictions with the correct class.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: Accuracy, recall, precision, and related metrics. https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification/accuracy-precision-recall
questions.convention: TP and TN count true positives and true negatives. FP and FN count false positives and false negatives.

questions.clue:
TP / (TP + FP)
Confusion-matrix counts.
questions.explanation: Precision measures the share of positive predictions that are correct.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: Accuracy, recall, precision, and related metrics. https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification/accuracy-precision-recall
questions.convention: TP and FP count true positives and false positives. Assumes at least one positive prediction.

questions.clue:
ŷ = b₀ + b₁x
One numeric feature predicts a numeric outcome.
questions.explanation: The fitted slope multiplies the feature and the intercept shifts the predicted outcome.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §3.1.1, Estimating the Coefficients. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue:
max(0, z)
Which activation function is this?
questions.explanation: ReLU outputs zero for negative inputs and passes positive inputs through unchanged.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Neural networks: Activation functions, Common activation functions. https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/neural-networks/activation-functions#common-activation-functions

questions.clue: A function estimates the remaining cost from a search state to a goal.
questions.explanation: The estimate can prioritize states that appear cheaper to complete from.
questions.reference: Stanford CS 221, Search 2, A* search and heuristic functions. https://web.stanford.edu/class/archive/cs/cs221/cs221.1192/lectures/search2-6pp.pdf

questions.clue: A training feature encodes the outcome using information available only after prediction time.
questions.explanation: The field would be unavailable at prediction time and can carry information about the target.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Production ML systems: Monitoring pipelines, Check for label leakage. https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/production-ml-systems/monitoring#check_for_label_leakage

questions.clue: A representative location is the arithmetic mean of all feature vectors assigned to that cluster.
questions.explanation: The centroid averages feature values coordinate by coordinate.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §12.4.1, K-Means Clustering. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue: What fraction measures how much of the data’s total variance one principal component captures?
questions.explanation: This proportion compares a component’s variance with the sum of all component variances.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §12.2.3, The Proportion of Variance Explained. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue: In a transformer, queries, keys and values are all computed from the same sequence of representations.
questions.explanation: Self-attention relates positions within one sequence. Cross-attention uses keys and values from another sequence.
questions.reference: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing, 3rd ed. draft (August 2026), Ch. 7, Transformers and Pretraining. https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/7.pdf

questions.clue: Apply the chain rule from a network’s loss back through its layers to obtain parameter gradients.
questions.explanation: Backpropagation efficiently computes gradients used by an optimization step.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Neural Networks: Training using backpropagation. https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/neural-networks/backpropagation

questions.clue: A route planner always expands the route with the smallest cost so far. Road costs vary and are positive.
questions.explanation: Uniform-cost search orders the frontier by accumulated path cost.
questions.reference: Stanford CS 221, Search 1, Uniform cost search. https://web.stanford.edu/class/archive/cs/cs221/cs221.1196/lectures/search1-6pp.pdf

questions.clue: Start with known facts. Whenever the premises of a rule are known, add its conclusion and continue.
questions.explanation: Forward chaining starts from facts and derives every conclusion supported by applicable rules.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley CS 188 course notes, §10.6, Forward Chaining. https://inst.eecs.berkeley.edu/~cs188/textbook/logic/forward.html

questions.clue: Photos of the same object come from many views. Keep all views of an object in a single fold.
questions.explanation: Holding entire objects together keeps their other views out of training when the object is evaluated.
questions.reference: scikit-learn documentation, GroupKFold, non-overlapping groups. https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.GroupKFold.html

questions.clue: Train trees on bootstrap samples and try a fresh random subset of features at each split.
questions.explanation: A random forest adds random feature selection at splits to reduce correlation among trees.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §8.2.2, Random Forests. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue: Start with one cluster per customer, then repeatedly merge the closest clusters into a hierarchy.
questions.explanation: Agglomerative clustering builds the hierarchy from the smallest groups upward.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §12.4.2, Hierarchical Clustering. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue: A writing model adds one token at a time, conditioning each prediction on all earlier tokens it can see.
questions.explanation: Each generated token joins the context for the next token prediction.
questions.reference: Jurafsky and Martin, Speech and Language Processing, 3rd ed. draft (August 2026), Ch. 7, Transformers and Pretraining. https://web.stanford.edu/~jurafsky/slp3/7.pdf

questions.clue:
Priority = g(n) + h(n)
g is cost from the start, h estimated cost to the goal.
questions.explanation: A* prioritizes the sum of cost already incurred and estimated cost to finish.
questions.reference: Stanford CS 221, Search 2, A* search and heuristic functions. https://web.stanford.edu/class/archive/cs/cs221/cs221.1192/lectures/search2-6pp.pdf

questions.clue:
TP / (TP + FN)
Confusion-matrix counts.
questions.explanation: Recall is the share of actual positives the classifier finds.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: Accuracy, recall, precision, and related metrics. https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification/accuracy-precision-recall
questions.convention: TP and FN count true positives and false negatives. Assumes at least one actual positive.

questions.clue:
p = 1 / [1 + exp(−z)]
z is the fitted linear score for a binary outcome.
questions.explanation: The sigmoid turns log odds into a probability between zero and one.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §4.3.1, The Logistic Model. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue:
Σᵢ ‖xᵢ − μ[c(i)]‖²
μc(i) is the mean of the cluster assigned to xᵢ.
questions.explanation: The objective sums squared distances from observations to their assigned cluster means.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §12.4.1, K-Means Clustering. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue: In a deterministic two-player zero-sum game, choose the move whose worst opponent reply gives the best payoff.
questions.explanation: Minimax assumes the opponent will choose the reply least favorable to the current player.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley CS 188 course notes, §3.2, Minimax. https://inst.eecs.berkeley.edu/~cs188/textbook/games/minimax.html

questions.clue: Skip branches whose available bounds show they cannot change the minimax value.
questions.explanation: Alpha-beta pruning avoids evaluating irrelevant branches while preserving the exact minimax value.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley CS 188 course notes, §3.2.1, Alpha-Beta Pruning. https://inst.eecs.berkeley.edu/~cs188/textbook/games/minimax.html

questions.clue: Among cases with similar predicted event probabilities, the observed event rate matches those probabilities.
questions.explanation: Calibration asks whether forecast probabilities agree with observed frequencies.
questions.reference: scikit-learn User Guide, Probability calibration, Calibration curves. https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/calibration.html#calibration-curves

questions.clue: This classifier maximizes a separating margin while penalizing permitted margin violations.
questions.explanation: The soft margin trades a wide margin against the cost of margin violations on the training examples.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §9.2.2, Details of the Support Vector Classifier. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue: Build clusters from connected dense neighborhoods and mark sparse points outside them as noise.
questions.explanation: DBSCAN grows clusters from dense regions and can leave isolated observations unassigned.
questions.reference: Ester et al. (1996), A Density-Based Algorithm for Discovering Clusters in Large Spatial Databases with Noise, §§3–4. https://cdn.aaai.org/KDD/1996/KDD96-037.pdf

questions.clue: During training, block each token position from attending to later positions in the same sequence.
questions.explanation: A causal mask preserves the left-to-right information available when predicting the next token.
questions.reference: Vaswani et al. (2017), Attention Is All You Need, §3.1, Encoder and Decoder Stacks. https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762#S3.SS1

questions.clue: A scheduling solver chooses the next unassigned task by finding the one with the fewest legal time slots remaining.
questions.explanation: The most constrained unassigned variable is considered first.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley CS 188 course notes, §2.4, Ordering. https://inst.eecs.berkeley.edu/~cs188/textbook/csp/ordering.html

questions.clue: After fitting a tree, the next tree fits the negative loss gradients of the current ensemble on the training cases.
questions.explanation: Gradient boosting builds an additive model by fitting successive corrections to reduce the loss.
questions.reference: Friedman (2001), Greedy Function Approximation: A Gradient Boosting Machine, Algorithm 1. https://doi.org/10.1214/aos/1013203451

questions.clue: Before PCA, put measurements in meters and kilograms on comparable scales so raw units have less influence.
choices: Sort the rows by feature value
questions.explanation: Centering and scaling each feature by its standard deviation avoids dominance from its original units.
questions.reference: James et al. (2023), An Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in Python, §12.2.4, More on PCA, Scaling the Variables. https://datamineaz.org/textbooks/jamesISL.pdf

questions.clue: A team estimates feature means and scales from all rows before cross-validation. What flaw does this introduce?
questions.explanation: Validation rows influence the learned transform. Fit it separately on each training fold.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley STAT 154, Cross Validation, §5.1, Example: using the validation data without noticing. https://stat154.berkeley.edu/fall-2026/labs/lab4_cross_val/lab4_presentation_2026.html

questions.clue: Two clusterings use different label numbers. Which measure compares membership pairs and adjusts for chance?
questions.explanation: The adjusted Rand index compares pair memberships, ignores label names, and corrects for chance.
questions.reference: scikit-learn User Guide, Clustering, Rand index. https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html#rand-index

questions.clue: A question-answering system retrieves manual passages for each query and feeds them to its text generator.
questions.explanation: Retrieved passages provide additional context for generation at query time.
questions.reference: Lewis et al. (2020), Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks, §2, Methods. https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2020/file/6b493230205f780e1bc26945df7481e5-Paper.pdf

questions.clue:
V*(s) = maxₐ E[r + γV*(s′) ∣ s,a]
r is reward, s′ the next state.
choices: Bellman equation for a fixed policy
questions.explanation: The optimum takes the best action’s expected immediate reward plus discounted future value.
questions.reference: UC Berkeley CS 188 course notes, §4.2, Solving Markov Decision Processes, Bellman equation. https://inst.eecs.berkeley.edu/~cs188/textbook/mdp/solve.html

questions.clue:
softmax(QKᵀ / √d) V
Q, K, V are queries, keys and values. d is key dimension.
questions.explanation: The scaled query-key similarities determine the weights applied to the values.
questions.reference: Vaswani et al. (2017), Attention Is All You Need, §3.2.1, Scaled Dot-Product Attention. https://arxiv.org/html/1706.03762#S3.SS2.SSS1

questions.clue:
2PR / (P + R)
P is precision and R is recall.
questions.explanation: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall.
questions.reference: Google Machine Learning Crash Course, Classification: Accuracy, recall, precision, and related metrics. https://developers.google.com/machine-learning/crash-course/classification/accuracy-precision-recall
questions.convention: Assumes precision and recall are defined and P + R is positive.

questions.clue:
[b(i) − a(i)] / max[a(i), b(i)]
a is mean within-cluster distance, b is the lowest mean distance to another cluster.
questions.explanation: Silhouette compares how close an observation is to its own cluster and to its nearest alternative cluster.
questions.reference: scikit-learn User Guide, Clustering, Silhouette Coefficient. https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/clustering.html#silhouette-coefficient
questions.convention: Assumes at least two clusters and a non-singleton cluster for the observation. Exclude the observation itself from a.
